newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Canada appoint negotiators in salmon fracas.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Canada appoint negotiators in salmon fracas.

text.p: The United States and Canada named new negotiators on Friday to try to resolve their simmering dispute over Pacific salmon.

President Bill Clinton chose William Ruckelshaus, former head of the Environmental Protection Agency, while the Canadian government named University of British Columbia President and Chancellor David Strangway.

Negotiations over the interpretation and implementation of the Pacific Salmon Treaty, signed in 1985, had snarled down under two previous negotiators, Mary-Beth West for the United States and Yves Fortier for Canada.

After Canadian fishing boats blockaded an Alaskan ferry for three days in Prince Rupert, British Columbia, to back their protest against alleged U.S. overfishing, the two sides agreed on Wednesday to restart talks.
The representatives will report directly to Clinton and Prime Minister Jean Chretien.
